questions.question: What is a complete circuit? Explain why a bulb does not light with only one wire.
questions.expected_answer: A complete circuit is a closed, unbroken pathway from one terminal of the energy source, through the wires and the device, and back to the other terminal. With only one wire, there is no pathway back to the cell, so electricity cannot flow and the bulb does not light.

questions.question: Name three faults that can stop a circuit from working, and how to fix each.
questions.expected_answer: A crocodile clip on the plastic covering instead of the bare metal: clip onto the metal. A bulb that is loose: screw it in firmly. A blown bulb with a broken filament: replace it. A flat cell: replace it with a good one. Check one component at a time.

questions.question: How does a switch work? What do open and closed mean?
questions.expected_answer: A switch breaks or completes a circuit. When it is closed, its metal parts touch, the circuit is complete and the device is on. When it is open, there is a gap, the circuit is broken and the device is off. A switch does not make electricity; it only opens or closes the pathway.
